title: Report on our floating market visit
text:
Class 5B visit to a floating market in South Kalimantan

Introduction

On Thursday, our class travelled by bus and then by boat to the Lok Baintan floating market, on the Martapura River. We went to find out how people buy and sell goods on the water and to compare it with our own market at home. This report explains what we saw.

What we saw

We reached the river at half past five in the morning, when the sky was still pink. By then, dozens of narrow wooden boats called jukung were gathered together, bumping gently against each other. Most of the traders were women who wore wide, round hats made of woven palm leaves, which protected them from the sun and the rain.

Each boat was a small shop. We saw one piled with bananas and pineapples, another with sacks of rice, and a third with sticky cakes wrapped in leaves. Customers paddled their own boats alongside, called out a price, and often bargained for a few minutes before agreeing. The buyers passed money across the water, and the sellers passed back the goods and the change.

What we found out

A trader named Ibu Rahmah told us that many families have sold goods this way for generations. Before there were good roads, she explained, the river was the only way to reach other villages, so the market grew up on the water. By about nine o'clock the boats start to leave, because the sun becomes too hot.

Conclusion

The floating market is a lively and friendly place. It is also, in our opinion, the most interesting kind of market in the region. However, fewer young people are learning to sell on the river, so the tradition may become less common. We recommend that visitors arrive early, buy something from the traders and ask before taking photographs.
